title: Deepfakes and How to Spot Them

scenes.text: A video of a famous actor promoting a scam investment app. [1] A voice call from your cousin, begging for money urgently. [2] Both could be fake, made by AI. Let's understand deepfakes, and how to spot them.

A deepfake is fake media made with AI, [1] that shows a real person saying or doing something they never did. [2] It can be a video, an image, or a voice. [3] The word comes from deep learning, plus fake.

data.definition: AI-generated video, image or audio that makes a real person appear to say or do something they never did.

scenes.text: There are three common types. [1] Face swap, putting one person's face on another person's body. [2] Voice cloning, copying someone's voice from just a short audio sample. [3] And lip sync, changing a real video, so the mouth matches new words.

Here's how deepfakes are misused. [1] Scam calls, with a cloned voice of a family member, or a boss. [2] Fake celebrity ads, promoting fraud investment apps. [3] And fake political videos, spreading misinformation before elections.

So how can you spot one? [1] Look at the face edges, and hair, for blurring or flickering. [2] Watch the eyes, and blinking. They can look odd. [3] Check if the lips match the words exactly. [4] Listen for flat, robotic emotion, or strange breathing. [5] Most importantly, check the source. Is it from an official account?

Here's a common myth. [1] People think they can always spot a deepfake with their eyes. [2] The best fakes now look and sound very real. Visual clues help, but checking the source, and verifying through another channel, is far more reliable.

data.myth: You can always spot a deepfake with your eyes.
data.fact: The best fakes look real. Checking the source and verifying another way is far more reliable.

scenes.text: Here's your safety plan for calls. [1] Pause. Scammers create urgency, so slow down. [2] Hang up, and call the person back, on the number you already have. [3] And agree on a family code word, that only you know.

Quick quiz! Your 'cousin' calls, asking for urgent money. What should you do first? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] Hang up, and call them back on the number you already have!

data.question: An urgent money call. First step?
options: Hang up and call them back on their known number

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] Deepfakes are AI-made fake video, images, or voices. [2] Types include face swap, voice clone, and lip sync. [3] Look for clues, but always verify the source.
